summary: Setup is moderate: the developer signs up, creates an app and can connect any X user right away, but API use is paid by prepaid credits. The main thing that can hold up launch is that X reviews every proposed use case and requires prior approval for AI-generated replies, and API calls stop when the credit balance runs out.
timeToProduction: ~1 hour to a few days, plus any X use-case review
cost: Pay-per-usage credits, for example $0.005 per Post read and $0.015 per Post created; no subscription
handoff: An agent can choose the scopes and build the authorize link with PKCE; you sign in to X, create the app, copy the secret into your server, approve the test login and run the code exchange on your server.

gates.title: Sign-up is self-serve: sign in, accept the Developer Agreement and describe your use
No test or unpublished mode is mentioned
X reviews proposed uses; AI-generated replies need prior approval
gates.what: X reviews every proposed use of the platform. AI-generated replies need X's approval before deployment.
gates.where: Developer account application in console.x.com; for AI replies, the Policy Support form (developer acts)
gates.todo: Describe the use case accurately. If the app posts AI-generated replies, request approval before launch.

gates.title: API use requires prepaid credits
gates.what: The API is pay-per-usage. Requests are blocked if the credit balance goes negative, and Post reads are capped at 3 million per monthly billing cycle.
gates.where: Developer Console → billing and credits; the developer acts

gates.title: Use case must stay compliant and up to date
gates.what: The developer must update the disclosed use case, and X may suspend or revoke access for policy violations. X may also audit compliance once a year.
gates.where: Developer Policy and Developer Guidelines; the developer acts
gates.todo: Notify X and get approval before changing the use case.

requirements.text: An X account to sign in to the Developer Console
A written description of the intended use of the API
A payment card for prepaid API credits

steps.text: Your agent decides scopes: read-only apps need tweet.read and users.read; posting adds tweet.write; add offline.access for a refresh token.
steps.why: Without offline.access, the access token lasts two hours.

attempt.text: Picked the scopes for an agent that reads and posts as the user.

steps.text: console.x.com: sign in with your X account, accept the Developer Agreement, click New App and enter a name and description.

attempt.text: This needs your X login, and X has no way to create an app outside its console.

steps.text: App settings → Authentication settings: enable OAuth 2.0 and choose the app type: Web App or Automated App (bot) is a confidential client; Native App or Single page App is a public client.
App settings → Authentication settings: add your callback URL.
steps.detail: The redirect_uri in the authorize URL must match exactly.

steps.text: App → Keys and Tokens: copy the Client ID, and the Client Secret if shown, into your secret store.
steps.why: The Client ID goes into the authorize URL.
steps.detail: Credentials are shown only once; save them immediately.

steps.text: Build the authorize link from your client ID, callback URL and scopes, plus a random state and a PKCE code_challenge.
steps.detail: Base URL: https://x.com/i/oauth2/authorize. The code_challenge is a fresh random secret for each login; code_challenge_method is S256 or plain.

attempt.text: Built the link with a fresh PKCE pair. It opens X's Authorize app page. Swap in your Client ID and callback URL.

steps.text: Browser: open the authorize link, log in to X and approve the app.
Your server: exchange the code at https://api.x.com/2/oauth2/token with the code_verifier, within 30 seconds.
steps.detail: X requires the code_verifier that matches the link's code_challenge.

blockers.problem: Requests are blocked with a negative credit balance.
blockers.fix: Add credits to cover the negative balance.

blockers.problem: The authorization code expires 30 seconds after it is issued.
blockers.fix: Exchange the code for an access token immediately.

blockers.problem: The callback URL must match exactly.
blockers.fix: Copy the callback URL from the app settings into redirect_uri without changes.

blockers.problem: Access tokens expire after two hours without offline.access.
blockers.fix: Request offline.access and use the refresh token flow.
